title: Reconcile attempts on daemon restart instead of purging every worker
description:
Objective: stop a daemon restart from yanking a task away from a CLI that is still running. packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:501 calls purgeAllWorkers on every start, and state/workerStore.ts:305 deletes every worker record and releases their tasks without first establishing that the external processes exited. A restart during a long build therefore hands live work to someone else.

Deliverable: on startup, attempts in phase running are moved to reconciling rather than being destroyed, and their tasks are held from reassignment while reconciling. A runner reattaches by presenting its attempt id plus process start time and host; a successful reattach returns the attempt to running. An attempt confirmed dead, or one that stays unreattached past a configurable reconcile window, is closed and gets exactly one successor generation.

Not in scope: heartbeat semantics, which are the sibling task. Preserve stable worker identity across the restart by persisting it separately from the attempt, and preserve the existing rule that a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker: the reconcile window must not become an idle-based auto-release for WORKING or PLANNING.

Unskips the acceptance case "restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership".

Verification: npx vitest run src/state/workerStore.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: Daemon startup moves running attempts to reconciling and holds their tasks from reassignment instead of releasing them
A runner that reattaches with a matching attempt id, process start time and host returns the attempt to running and keeps the task assigned
An attempt confirmed dead, or unreattached past the configurable reconcile window, is closed and permits exactly one successor generation
Stable worker identity survives the restart and is persisted separately from the attempt record
The reconcile window is a settings key with a documented default and is never applied to a live reattached attempt, so no idle-based auto-release is introduced for WORKING or PLANNING
The acceptance case for restart during a long build is unskipped and passes unchanged
npx vitest run src/state/workerStore.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Do not reintroduce idle-based auto-release for WORKING or PLANNING; a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker.
REVIEW's existing reviewStaleTimeoutMs self-heal stays exactly as it is.
Reassignment must establish the old process stopped, or contain its writes; a JSON record alone does not stop a running CLI.

CONTRACT:
- New tool moe.reattach_attempt {taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt, host}. Called over the REAL MCP wire (ws /mcp) against a spawned daemon child running `_run` through tsx — not a StateManager reload. 240s budget, real long-build process.
- Success: attempt phase `running`, task-L stays WORKING + assignedWorkerId worker-W, worker file currentTaskId 'task-L'. Exactly one attempt record throughout (no successor).
- Refusal 1 (identity): processStartedAt off by 60s, and separately a different host with the same start time -> code -32002, codeName ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, tool 'moe.reattach_attempt'.
- Refusal 2 (competing claim): claim_next_task {statuses:['WORKING'], taskId:'task-L', workerId:'worker-X'} -> -32002, codeName ATTEMPT_RECONCILING, tool 'moe.claim_next_task', message CONTAINS 'attempt-L-1' (MoeError.context is NOT forwarded over the wire; McpAdapter.ts:310-315 forwards only {code, message, data:{tool, codeName}}).
- The `tool` field toolRefusal asserts is auto-populated by McpAdapter from params.name for any thrown MoeError — no per-tool work needed, but the refusal MUST be a thrown MoeError, not a returned object.
- Byte-purity: holdBytes captured after daemon #2 startup; task/worker/attempt files must be byte-identical after EVERY refusal, and listRecords(attempts).length stays 1.
- IDEMPOTENCE: daemon #1 reattaches before any kill. After my startup reconcile pass daemon #1 will have parked it in `reconciling`, so reattach must handle reconciling->running AND running->running (no-op). Both are asserted as `running`.
- LIVENESS: worker-W lastActivityAt is 3h old and the build emits nothing. Nothing in this work may consult lastActivityAt.

implementationPlan.description: RECONCILE ON STARTUP INSTEAD OF DESTROYING. Add one exported helper to packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts that moves every attempt currently in the running phase to reconciling, reusing the existing phase setter so the store keeps its single write-then-publish ordering, and returning what it moved so the caller can decide which workers to spare. Give it a comment stating plainly what the phase means: the daemon has lost sight of this execution and is holding the task until a runner proves the process is still there, which is not the same as believing it is alive. Then change `purgeAllWorkers` in src/state/workerStore.ts. It currently deletes every worker file, clears the map and releases every orphaned assignment. It must now spare a worker that owns a non-closed attempt: keep its record on disk and in the map, keep its currentTaskId, and leave its task WORKING and assigned rather than routing it through the release path. The worker record is what the definition of done means by stable identity persisted separately from the attempt, so it is deliberately not derived from the attempt file. Every worker with no attempt, or only closed ones, keeps today's purge and release behaviour exactly, because that is the legacy path for every project that predates attempts. Keep the existing per-worker error handling: one unwritable record must not abort startup for the rest of the fleet. In src/index.ts, at the startup call site around line 501, run the reconcile pass before the purge so the purge can see which attempts were held, and confirm while you are there that the state load which populates the attempts map already runs before both. Nothing here may consult lastActivityAt or any other idle signal.

Its comment states what the phase means: the daemon has LOST SIGHT of this execution and holds the task until a runner proves which process it is talking about — which is not a belief that the process is alive, and not a belief that it is dead.

workerStore.ts: new private `workersHoldingOpenAttempts(state)` builds the spared set from attempt phases only (never lastActivityAt, never any idle signal). `purgeAllWorkers` now:

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE STEP'S LETTER, flagged deliberately: the team-memberIds clear at the end of the purge wiped ALL members. Left as-is it would evict a spared worker from its team and tombstone it, so `getTeamForWorker` would return null on its next call and the claim path would re-derive its role from statuses — identity loss on the exact seat the hold exists to protect. It now evicts only the non-spared ids, keeps spared ids in memberIds, tombstones only the evicted, and skips the write entirely when nothing is evicted (byte-purity). The acceptance fixture's worker has no team, so this is not test-driven — it is the hold being coherent.

implementationPlan.description: REFUSE A COMPETING CLAIM WHILE AN ATTEMPT IS RECONCILING. In src/tools/claimNextTask.ts add a refusal that mirrors the finalizing one already in that file: same position, inside the exclusive section and before any ranking, eligibility scan or assignment write, so a refused claim can never have changed an owner. It differs in scope, and the difference matters: the finalizing hold is scoped to the calling worker, while this one is scoped to the TASK, because the whole point is to stop a DIFFERENT worker taking a task whose owner is still out there. Throw a MoeError with the STATE_CONFLICT code, codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_RECONCILING`, a message naming the attempt id, and a context carrying the attempt id, its generation, the task and the holding worker. Follow whatever the finalizing refusal does to surface the `tool` field that the acceptance helper asserts, so both refusals look the same on the wire. Do not let this refusal fire for the attempt's own owner reattaching through the claim path: reattachment has its own tool and this refusal is for third parties. Change nothing about claimable statuses, dependency gating, ranking, the alreadyAssigned resume or the attempt opening that already exists in this file. This is the error handling path the acceptance case exercises with worker-X, and it asserts the files are byte-identical afterwards, so the refusal must happen before any write.

implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE REATTACH TOOL. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reattachAttempt.ts following the shape of the neighbouring tool modules: an exported factory returning a ToolDefinition named `moe.reattach_attempt`, an input schema declaring taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt and host with additionalProperties false, and a handler whose whole body runs inside state.runExclusive. Do NOT mark it blocking: it never parks. Handler order: validate the inputs and refuse malformed ones as invalid input; load the attempt by id and refuse a missing one or one whose taskId does not match, by name; then compare the presented identity against the stored record. The identity is the attempt id, the generation, the recorded processStartedAt and the recorded host, and ALL of them must match: the acceptance case refuses a start time off by sixty seconds and refuses a different host with the same start time, both with codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` and the STATE_CONFLICT code. Compare the timestamps as exact recorded strings rather than by parsing to a date, so a re-serialised value cannot widen the match. On a mismatch throw before any write, because the case asserts byte-identical files afterwards. On a match, move the attempt to running through the store's phase setter and return the attempt id, generation and phase; an attempt already running is a no-op that returns the same success, which is what the first daemon in the case relies on. Leave the task and the worker record alone: the point of the hold is that they were never disturbed, and writing them here would be a second source of truth. Say in a comment what this tool does and does not prove: a matching process start time and host narrow which process the runner is talking about, they do not establish that it is alive, and nothing may treat them as proof. Then register the tool in getTools() in src/tools/index.ts, because an unregistered tool is silently invisible to MCP.

   Read all three before touching anything. They pin the OLD purge-everything contract — each seeds a worker record PLUS a running attempt and asserts the task is released and the attempt closed, which is exactly what this card's DoD replaces ("holds their tasks from reassignment instead of releasing them"). Not a regression; a contract these tests pinned.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW — every checklist item confirmed, two real defects found and FIXED.

CONFIRMED FROM THE DIFF:
- A worker owning a non-closed attempt survives startup: file skipped in the unlink loop (`spared.has(path.basename(file,'.json'))`), map entry restored from the SURVIVING MAP OBJECT (not re-read, so never rewritten), currentTaskId intact. Its task never enters the release path because `isTaskAssignedToMissingWorker` is false once the seat is back in the map, so it is neither released nor re-routed and `closeOpenAttempts` is never reached for it.
- A worker with no attempt, or only closed ones, keeps the original delete + nextStatusForRelease behaviour. Pinned by two store cases plus the three repointed releaseTask cases.
- NO idle signal anywhere. Grepped the added lines: `lastActivityAt` appears only inside comments saying it must not be used; no `isWorkerAlive`, no `Date.now()`, no window/timeout in any changed production path.
- The reconciling refusal is scoped BY TASK (`listAttempts(state, params.taskId).find(phase === 'reconciling')`), not by caller, with the owner exempt. VERIFIED the ranked pool needs no change rather than assuming it: `isTaskClaimable` = unassigned OR assigned-to-inactive (missing/DEAD), and a spared owner is present and not DEAD, so a held row is never offered.
- Both refusals throw before any write; store and acceptance cases assert the files afterwards (byte-level in the acceptance case, phase+assignment in the unit cases).
- Identity requires attempt id + generation + processStartedAt + host, timestamp compared as the EXACT stored string — pinned by a case presenting the same instant as `2026-09-11T12:15:30.123+03:00` and still being refused.
- Already-running reattach is a byte-identical no-op, pinned on the file bytes.
- Registered in getTools() and NOT blocking — both asserted in a test, not just read.
- Sibling card untouched: no reconcile window, no successor generation, no sweep. `sweeps.ts` has zero changes.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED (neither had a failing test; this is what the review caught):
1. `reconcileRunningAttempts` had no per-attempt error handling, so ONE unwritable attempt record would throw out of `startDaemon`'s init try/catch and BRICK DAEMON STARTUP — strictly worse than the old behaviour, and a violation of the same rail the purge already honours. Now a per-attempt try/catch that logs and continues. It fails in the safe direction: a record that cannot move stays `running`, which is still non-closed, so its seat is still spared and its task still held. New store case `survives an attempt it cannot park` injects the write failure and asserts exactly that.
2. `workerId`/`runnerId` are validated but deliberately NOT compared, and nothing said so. `claim_next_task` opens attempts with `runnerId = workerId`, so comparing the runner's own id would refuse every genuine reattach — the exact trap a named regression test already pins for finalize_attempt. Added the comment AND a regression case that reattaches an attempt stored with `runnerId = 'worker-W'` while presenting `runnerId = 'runner-session-42'` and still succeeds, so nobody "tightens" the identity into something no runner can satisfy.

Other angles checked, no action needed: concurrency (whole reattach handler and the claim refusal are inside `state.runExclusive`; `reconcileRunningAttempts` iterates an Array snapshot from `listAttempts`, so the concurrent map mutation is safe); inputs (every string non-blank-validated, generation must be a positive safe integer, `additionalProperties:false`; the attempt id is only a map key and `writeEntity` already guards path traversal); an attempt whose workerId differs from the task's assignee still releases and closes correctly, since the seat holding the row is the one that is gone; a second restart over an already-`reconciling` attempt is a no-op that keeps the hold.

FILE COUNT: 12, not the plan's 9. The three deltas are each flagged, none is drift: `util/claimGuards.ts` (the refusal belongs beside the finalizing one, and the plan's own step-4 text told me to mirror it); `tools/reattachAttempt.test.ts` (repo convention is a sibling test per tool module — a new MCP tool with no unit tests is what QA would flag); `tools/releaseTask.test.ts` (three cases pinning the old purge-everything contract, which step 7 explicitly anticipated).

FOREIGN DIRTY PATHS — NOT MINE, NOT TOUCHED: `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts` and `createTask.test.ts` appeared in this shared checkout during my session and belong to another worker. I did not revert, stage or modify them.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Planning all seven definition-of-done items in one card: it needed 10 distinct files, the size gate's hard ceiling, with a real-process acceptance case that takes minutes. The operator was asked and chose to split, so the give-up half is now task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c and this card keeps exactly what its acceptance case drives. (2) Deriving worker identity from the attempt record rather than sparing the worker file: rejected, because the definition of done asks for identity persisted SEPARATELY from the attempt, and the acceptance case asserts the worker file's currentTaskId directly after the restart. (3) Scoping the reconciling claim refusal to the calling worker, mirroring the finalizing hold: rejected outright, and worth stating because it is the obvious copy-paste error — the finalizing hold stops a worker starting more work, while this one stops a DIFFERENT worker taking a task whose owner is still out there, so it must be scoped by task. (4) Parsing the recorded process start time to a date before comparing: rejected, since a re-serialised value could widen the match; compare the exact stored string. (5) Having reattach also rewrite the task or worker record: rejected, because the whole claim of the hold is that neither was disturbed, and writing them would create a second source of truth. (6) Consulting lastActivityAt to decide whether to hold: forbidden by a task rail and by the fixture, whose worker has been quiet for three hours and must still keep its task.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The acceptance case at line 1607 is the real specification and is already in the tree. It drives the genuine startup path through a spawned daemon child rather than a StateManager reload, spawns a real silent build process, kills the daemon abruptly, and asserts byte-identical task, worker and attempt files across every refusal. It requires a tool this card's description never names, `moe.reattach_attempt`, with the full identity tuple. Its `toolRefusal` helper asserts a `tool` field on the error alongside code and codeName, so both refusals must carry it the way the existing finalizing refusal does. The first daemon in the case reattaches an attempt that is already running, which pins reattach as idempotent for that phase. On the production side, purgeAllWorkers at workerStore.ts line 305 deletes every worker file, clears the map and releases assignments through nextStatusForRelease, with a deliberate per-worker try/catch so one bad record cannot abort startup; its call site is src/index.ts line 501, and the state load that populates the attempts map runs before it. The attempt store's phase setter already treats a repeated phase as a no-op and closed as terminal, so reconciling and running transitions need no new store primitive beyond one pass helper. src/state/sweeps.ts exists and is where the sibling card's window belongs, not here. src/state/workerStore.test.ts does not exist yet and this card's verification command names it, so it is created here.
planningNotes.risks: The single most likely defect is scoping the reconciling refusal by worker instead of by task, because the finalizing refusal directly above it does exactly that and reads as the pattern to copy. Second is reintroducing a liveness inference: any lastActivityAt check added to the hold passes casual review and fails the three-hour-quiet fixture, and a task rail forbids it. Third is the byte-purity requirement: the case compares raw file bytes after each refusal, so a stray activity row, timestamp or defensive rewrite anywhere in the refusal path breaks it. Sparing a worker from the purge changes a path every other test boots through, so watch the full suite rather than just the named files. The acceptance case spawns real processes with a 240 second budget; if the environment cannot spawn daemon children, that must be reported honestly rather than papered over. Finally, do not overstate the result: matching a process start time and host narrows which process a runner means and proves nothing about liveness, and until the sibling card lands a genuinely dead runner parks its task indefinitely — both belong in the completion summary.
